# Reliable Control of a Stochastic Agent — Deterministic-Layer Architecture

**Research pack:** 20260809T020632Z_reliable-control-deterministic-layer
**Date:** 2026-08-09
**Status:** Complete (Public/T2)

---

## 1. Direct Answer — The Architecture in One Page

You cannot reliably control the opaque stochastic middle of an LLM. You CAN build a deterministic shell around it. The architecture has four layers:

```
OPERATOR MODEL (persistent preferences → deterministic rules)
        ↓
TYPED CONTROL CHANNEL (note|veto|cancel|approve|pause|resume → process actions)
        ↓
BOUNDARY VERIFICATION GATES (byte-diff, invariant, spec_gate, fidelity score)
        ↓
SHRUNKEN STOCHASTIC BAND (frozen prefix + verkle-anchored spec + tool-graph restriction)
        ↓
[STOCHASTIC MODEL — narrow band, every output verified at boundary]
```

**The rule:** Control signals operate on the deterministic layer (process state, queue, job floor). Prose injection into the model is a probabilistic nudge — useful but not reliable. The persistent operator model translates operator preferences into deterministic rules so the system doesn't re-negotiate through the model on every turn.

**What this looks like in Mag today:** We have pieces of layers 2-4 (operator_inbox typed vocabulary emerging, write_file snapshot verification, verkle tip anchoring). The missing piece is layer 1: a persistent operator model that survives sessions and translates preferences into deterministic rules.
